summary: UCSB revises three earlier specifications. Support for the Online System network interface in RFC 74 was dropped because no site had used it. The remote job entry specification in RFC 105 no longer uses a message type byte. The file system specification in RFC 122 is also revised, in line with new host-host protocol changes.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 217 revises three UCSB service specifications. It retires the unused OLS specification and changes how RJE and RJOR establish connections and format their data.

questions: ucsb ols rje smfs specification changes
ucsb rje and rjor socket numbers
subtitle: A UCSB notice revising specifications for OLS, remote job services, and a file system.

tldr.problem: Three UCSB service specifications needed changes because the OLS software had no known network implementation and Host-Host protocol changes affected RJE and RJOR.
tldr.mechanism: The note declares the OLS specification obsolete, removes the message-type byte from RJE/RJOR, changes their listening sockets, and specifies byte sizes for service connections.
tldr.outcome: RFC 217 updates RFCs 105 and 122 and obsoletes RFC 74, as stated in the unit metadata and the RFC text.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 217's status as Unknown. It updates RFC 105 and RFC 122, and obsoletes RFC 74.

sections.title: The Three UCSB Specifications
sections.content:
RFC 217 revises specifications for the UCSB On-Line System (OLS), Remote Job Entry (RJE) and Remote Job Output Retrieval (RJOR), and the Simple-Minded File System (SMFS). The memo says that no network site was known to have written code to interface with the OLS software described in RFC 74, so UCSB ended support for it and declared RFC 74 obsolete.

The changes to RJE and RJOR apply to the specifications in RFC 105. The byte-size change also applies to SMFS, described in RFC 122.
sections.plainLanguage: The note updates three UCSB service specifications. It says the OLS software had no known network interface implementation, so its earlier specification was obsolete.

sections.title: Changes to RJE and RJOR Connections
sections.content:
Following changes to the Host-Host protocol, RJE and RJOR no longer send or expect 8 bits of zeros as the first byte on a connection. The message-type concept is removed from their specifications.

RJE and RJOR now use a standard Initial Connection Protocol to create a full-duplex connection to the user. They listen on sockets x'201' and x'301', respectively, instead of x'200' and x'300'. RJOR still uses a simplex connection to the user's receive socket when it calls the user back because a requested job's output is ready.
sections.plainLanguage: RJE and RJOR stop sending an initial zero byte and use new socket numbers. They use the standard connection procedure, while RJOR still sends its callback output over a one-way connection.

sections.title: Byte Sizes for Service Connections
sections.content: RJE/RJOR and SMFS specify a byte size of 8 for the connection to the user's receive socket. The user may choose the byte size for the other simplex connection, and UCSB accepts any valid byte size there.
sections.plainLanguage: The connection to the user's receive socket uses 8-bit bytes. For the other one-way connection, the user can choose any valid byte size.
